draft.title: Urban concentration in Australia
card: An urban area is a city or large town. Urbanisation is the growth in the share of a country's people who live in urban areas.
Most Australians live in cities. Around nine in ten people live in urban areas, which makes Australia one of the most urbanised countries in the world.
Urban concentration means that people are clustered in a few places. In Australia, most people live in the large capital cities, such as Sydney, Melbourne, Brisbane and Perth.
Most of these capital cities are on or near the coast. Large areas of inland Australia have very few people.
draft.remember: Australia is highly urbanised, and its people are concentrated in a few big coastal capitals.

a.q: Which statement best describes urban concentration in Australia?
opts: Most people live in a few large capital cities on the coast
Most people live on farms spread evenly across the inland
Most people live in many mid-sized cities across the country
Most people live in small towns in the centre of the continent
a.why: Australians are clustered in a few large capital cities, mostly on the coast. The option about many mid-sized cities is tempting, but it describes a spread-out pattern, not a concentrated one.
a.clue: Think about where the largest cities are and how many there are.

b.q: A map of Australia shows dots for where people live. Which pattern would the map most likely show?
opts: Dense clusters around coastal capitals and few dots inland
Dots spread evenly over the whole continent
Dense clusters in the middle with few dots on the coast
Many separate clusters of equal size across the inland
b.why: Most Australians live in a few large coastal capital cities, so the dots would cluster there. An even spread is wrong because large areas of the inland have very few people.
b.clue: Picture where Sydney, Melbourne and Perth are, compared with the inland.
